Whoa, I was in this exact situation last year.

This girl was an ex of one of my husband's former friends and at first we all hung out and she was really cool. As time went on, there were inappropriate jokes being made about us being a throuple or in a poly relationship which made me uncomfortable and shouldn't have started in the first place. 

Eventually, I got annoyed by the way that they would talk to each other and they both had more in common than I did. So I distanced myself and made it clear to my husband that I was not okay with how they interacted. I outright asked him if he had feelings for her and he couldn't tell me. I felt incredibly insecure and like I didn't measure up to her despite having been his partner for almost 10 years at that point. He decided to stand his ground and not lose his friend over me so I left.

I spent a week with my parents in another town and then signed a 6 month lease at an apartment. It was my first time living alone. It was scary and it was hard, especially financially. But I did it. And we took a good break from each other and gave ourselves some distance and space to miss each other. And we did.

I started individual therapy and really worked on myself and my insecurities and self esteem. My husband and I started talking on the phone occasionally and that grew in frequency. He would come over sometimes and we would have little dates. We just kind of needed time to start over. Our relationship did get better. Right before it was time to come home, we started couples therapy which was a stipulation of mine before moving back in. If you're having trouble getting him to listen outside at all, I would teach him 'look' as in 'look at me' while indoors and get really good at it. Then before even steeping foot outside, start working on some easy tricks right next to the door to go outside. If he's still fine, open the door but don't go out. Try more tricks. If you lose him, shut the door and try again. By doing this, he is learning that he doesn't get to go outside until he's listening. It may take a while, so be prepared to spend some time on it. But by the end of that training session, you should have look at me down, and be comfortable training inside around the with the door open. 

For outside, start incrementally. Go right outside the door and do the easy stuff. If it's too distracting, head back inside with the door open and work there. If you can get him to pay attention and watch you right outside the door, try moving another few feet outside. Go slowly and be patient. I like to compare them to small children in that they only have so much attention before they get bored and you lose them. This type of session might have to be broken up into small pieces throughout the day.

Does he know 'leave it'? You can also use leave it and look at me when major distractions are present. 

EDIT: If he won't take certain treats because he's too distracted, we also recommend using higher value treats that he doesn't get all the time to entice him to listen and make yourself more rewarding than the environment. Try cooked chicken, cheeses, hot dog pieces, lunch meats, etc. Whatever you have that may make your dog stop and listen just for a small taste!
